# CSS Gotchas

Known CSS patterns that cause silent rendering failures or hard-to-debug issues.

## Entries

- [Self-hosted @font-face fonts do not render inside iframe documents](iframe-font-face-rendering.md): WOFF2 fonts loaded via @font-face (URL, base64, data URI) never render inside iframes despite valid files and successful fetches. Use Google Fonts CDN link tags instead. HIGH.
- [Stylesheet load order decides equal-specificity wins; scope the selector when you can't rely on it](stylesheet-load-order-equal-specificity.md): Two runtime-injected sheets with equal-specificity rules resolve by load order, so a restyle in the first-loaded sheet silently loses to a global rule; rely on order deliberately or bump specificity with a scoping class (.dl .x beats .x). MEDIUM.
- [A CSS live-preview of a canvas drawImage composite must mirror drawImage exactly, not use object-fit:cover](canvas-preview-mirror-drawimage.md): object-fit:cover pre-crops the box so a pan can only slide the crop, not reveal more source -- the preview silently diverges from the server canvas. Render the img at natural size and apply the full translate(dx,dy) scale(es) that matches drawImage(img, dx, dy, iw*es, ih*es). MEDIUM.
- [A global `zoom` scale is usually MEDIA-GATED, so phone CSS is in real pixels](media-gated-zoom-scale-phone-real-px.md): `body { zoom: var(--ui-scale) }` is opted into at a desktop breakpoint, so on a phone the scale is 1 and a declared 40px paints at 40 real px -- but the design-system docs quote the desktop value as "the default", so reviewers multiply it in and sign off on undersized touch targets. Read the token in tokens.css, not the prose about it, and measure getBoundingClientRect() at 375px. HIGH.
- [`:where()` contributes ZERO specificity, so a rule written with it guarantees nothing](where-zero-specificity-guarantees-nothing.md): A `:where(button, [role="button"], .tab) { min-height: 44px }` accessibility floor sits at (0,0,1) and loses to every class rule, so it enforces the minimum only for elements nothing else styles -- present in the source, greppable, and inert. Ask whether the rule should WIN (never `:where()`) or LOSE (a reset that must yield); note `:is()` inflates to its most specific arm, while `:not()`/`:has()` do contribute their arguments' weight. HIGH.
- [A `var(--x)` naming a token that does not exist is silent, and WHICH property it breaks decides the symptom](undefined-custom-property-inherit-vs-initial.md): An undefined custom property makes the declaration Invalid At Computed-Value Time, which resolves to `unset` -- so an INHERITED property (color) takes the parent's value and merely looks slightly dim, while a NON-INHERITED one (transition) resets to initial, turning `transition: transform var(--nope)` into `transition: none` so the animation never runs. No linter has a rule for it (stylelint's custom-property-no-missing-var-function is the reverse check) and the static tree is usually outside tsconfig, so 45 dead references survived months with lint green. Gate it by diffing references against definitions -- only a BARE `var(--x)` is a bug, `var(--x, fallback)` is a legitimate optional knob, and `var(--a, var(--b))` is caught for free because the inner reference is itself bare. HIGH.
- [A utility class only exists on the pages whose stylesheet defines it](borrowed-class-unloaded-stylesheet.md): With per-route/per-section code-split sheets, a class borrowed from another section's stylesheet resolves to NOTHING -- no error, no lint, and the element still renders because it just inherits, so a mono utility silently drops to the body sans face. Same failure when rules are promoted to a shared sheet and renamed but one call site is missed. Audit by resolving each file's import graph to the sheets it can actually load; discount two false positives (shared JS whose markup never leaves one section, and modules that inject their own runtime `<style>`). HIGH.
